_comment: NSE Capital Market (cash equities) trading calendar. Every date below is transcribed from the NSE circular named beside it; nothing is inferred from BSE, from a prior year, or from a holiday pattern. Years not listed read UNKNOWN. Edit only from a new NSE circular, and add it to provenance.
source: NSE Capital Market Segment circulars NSE/CMTR/65587, 65729, 70319 (2025) and NSE/CMTR/71775, 72260, 72349 (2026)
segment: NSE Capital Market (CM) segment — equities. F&O, currency and commodity segments publish their own circulars and are not covered here.

verification.how: each circular PDF in provenance was fetched from nsearchives.nseindia.com on 2026-10-07 and read in full; its sha256 is recorded beside it
open_items: 2026-11-08 Muhurat: NSE has announced the session but not its hours; the day stays UNKNOWN until NSE's timing circular is read.

notes: Pre-open order entry runs 09:00-09:08 with matching to 09:15; it is modelled as PRE_OPEN 09:00-09:15 on special sessions exactly as on regular days (src/markets/venues.py XNSE).
A Muhurat or Budget session REPLACES the day's phases, including on a date that is also a listed holiday (2025-10-21).
POST_MARKET is NSE's post-closing / closing session (regular days 15:40-16:00; Muhurat 2025 14:55-15:05).
When NSE publishes the 2026 Muhurat timing circular, delete the 2026-11-08 unknown_days entry, add the session to special_sessions with its NSE/CMTR reference, and add the circular to provenance.
limitations: Years before 2025 and from 2027 read UNKNOWN: no NSE circular for them has been transcribed. NSE normally publishes the next year's list in December.
Ad-hoc closures NSE announces after 2026-10-07 (it notified 2026-01-15 three days ahead) are not here until this file is updated.
Mock and simulated sessions are not live trading and are deliberately absent.
cross_checks: exchange_calendars 4.13.2 XBOM (BSE, an independent source) lists exactly the same weekday closures for 2025 (14) and 2026 (16 = NSE/CMTR/71775's 15 + 2026-01-15). It records neither Muhurat session nor the 2026-02-01 Sunday session; it is NOT used to answer for NSE.
